display.title: Torah, the Best Thing of All, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: Pirates attack the ship and seize the merchants' riches, but Rabbi Akiva's treasure, his Torah, cannot be taken; the humbled merchants ask him to be their teacher.
display.summary_long: The second and final chapter of the story. Rabbi Akiva is studying Torah alone in his cabin when the captain cries that the ship is under attack. A band of pirates boards, lines the passengers up on deck under threat, and carries off all the merchants' precious goods while they watch helplessly. Only Rabbi Akiva looks calm. When the pirate leader asks whether it bothers him to be penniless, Rabbi Akiva explains that his possession is not gold or jewels but the Torah he has learned, which Dovid HaMelech called more precious than gold and silver and which can never be stolen. He even offers to share it by teaching the pirate. After the pirates leave, the merchants apologize for laughing at him, and many ask Rabbi Akiva to become their teacher so they too can own the most precious gift of all.
display.lesson: Torah is the most precious possession; it stays with you no matter what.
